title.narrative: Coastal Embankment Improvement Project - Phase I (CEIP-I)

description.narrative: The objectives of the First Phase of the Coastal Embankment Improvement Project for Bangladesh are to (a) increase the area protected in selected polders from tidal flooding and frequent storm surges, which are expected to worsen due to climate change; (b) improve agricultural production by reducing saline water intrusion in selected polders; and (c) improve the Government of Bangladesh?s capacity to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible crisis or emergency. The project has five components. (1) Rehabilitation and improvement of polders component will finance activities that aim to increase community resilience to tidal flooding and storm surges. (2) Implementation of social and environmental management frameworks and plans component will support consultation with and strengthening of polder stakeholders and beneficiaries. (3) Construction supervision, monitoring and evaluation of project and coastal zone monitoring component will cover consulting services for (i) surveys, designs of remaining polders to be included in the project and (ii) construction supervision of rehabilitation and improvement of coastal embankments; (iii) continuously monitoring project activities and providing feedback to the government and the implementing agency on the project?s performance. (4) Project management, technical assistance, training and strategic studies component will support Bangladesh Water Development Board in implementing the project. (5) Contingent emergency response component will be contingent upon the fulfillment of the following conditions: (i) the Government of Bangladesh has determined that an eligible crisis or emergency has occurred and the Bank has agreed and notified the Government; (ii) the Ministry of Finance has prepared and adopted the Contingent Emergency Response (CER) Implementation Plan that is agreed with the Bank; (iii) Bangladesh Water Development Board has prepared, adopted, and disclosed safeguards instruments required as per Bank guidelines for all activities from the CER Implementation Plan for eligible financing under the CERC.

The project development objectives are to (a) increase the area protected in selected polders from tidal flooding and frequent storm surges, which are expected to worsen due to climate change; (b) improve agricultural production by reducing saline water intrusionin selected polders; and (c) improve the Government of Bangladesh's capacity to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible crisis or emergency.

title.narrative: BWDB Person Days of training provided

comment.narrative: The actual (current) person-days training is the summation of the number of BWDB officials who completed training multiplied by the duration of training expressed in days. The project provided training to BWDB officials for different technical aspects, including modeling physical processes and other relevant phenomena (subsidence, climate change, river morphology, etc.), design, investment plan, feasibility study, project management, etc.

<p>Target achieved (100% achievement compared to the revised target: 10 compared to 10 WMAs). </p>

<p>Information source: BWDB project completion report and other supplementary documents. </p>

<p>Description of indicator was revised from “Water Management Organization (WMO)” to “Water Management Association (WMA)” during January 2020 restructuring. End target was also revised from 4 to 10. As per institutional requirement, each polder now has one WMA, there are 10 polders, accordinly, end target revised to 10. As per the initial project design, this was to be piloted only in a few polders, later formation of WMA required for all polders.</p>

End target achieved. Water Management Association (WMA) is the apex body of Water Management Groups (WMG) in a Polder with representatives from each WMGs. WMG is formed for each hydraulic boundary known as Water Management Unit (WMU) within a Polder. There are several WMUs in a Polder having WMG for each.

title.narrative: Detailed design of future 7 Polders (including EIA, RAP/LAP)

comment.narrative:
<p>Target achieved (100% achievement compared to the revised target: 7 compared to detailed design of  future 7 Polders, including EIA, RAP/LAP). </p>

<p>Information source: BWDB project completion report and other supplementary documents. </p>

<p>The Project’s scope was reduced from 17 to 10 polders due to the financing constraints. The remaining 7 polders would be moved to a potential second phase of the Project together with additional polders under design, the source of financing of the second phase is not yet determined. However, the detailed design of these 7 polders was ready as well as EIA, RAP/LAP are at final stage of preparation. This was part of the project scope, but was not reflected in the original results framework.</p>
